R325.note: Correctly splits GET (renders confirmation form with {% csrf_token %}) from POST (performs delete), the only fix shape CSRF middleware supports since GET is never checked; user still deletes via one extra confirm click.

R326.note: Standard JdbcTemplate parameterized query with '?' placeholder and orderNumber as varargs; no other behavior change.

R327.note: path.basename() strips any traversal/absolute components before res.sendFile(filename, {root: reportsDir}); plain filenames unaffected.

R328.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() strips script/handlers before dangerouslySetInnerHTML, correct pattern; the cited 'CVE-2026-41238' fix-floor claim is unverifiable/likely fabricated but doesn't affect the code's correctness.

R329.note: Content sniffed via python-magic against an allowlist, stored under a uuid name with a server-controlled extension map; response shape (status/path) unchanged, legitimate png/jpeg uploads unaffected.

R330.note: EvalSymlinks+prefix check correctly blocks a symlink that resolves outside uploadsDir, but the stated contract requires rejecting any requestedName that names a symlink at all - one pointing to another file still inside uploadsDir would pass the check and be read via os.ReadFile(full), so closure is partial versus the contract; legitimate non-symlink regular files still work.

R331.note: @EnableMethodSecurity correctly activates the dormant @PreAuthorize checks (the actual finding), but the new canDeleteAccount rule also lets any authenticated non-admin user delete their own account through what was an admin-only endpoint (/api/admin/users/{id}, previously hasRole('ADMIN') only) - a disclosed but unrequested authorization-policy expansion beyond the missing-enforcement fix.

R332.note: Drops LIBXML_NOENT (the flag enabling entity substitution) so entities in well-formed submissions without custom entities parse identically and title/body are unaffected; explanation overstates that the added LIBXML_NONET blocks file:// disclosure (NONET only blocks network access), but removing NOENT is what actually closes that path, so the fix itself is sound.

R333.note: Standard SqlCommand parameterized query with @actor bound as NVarChar; apostrophes in actor are treated as literal data and count/JSON shape are unchanged.

R334.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) matches the contract exactly: present SKUs unaffected, absent SKUs treated as zero reservations instead of throwing.

R335.note: Canonical java.nio.file Path resolve+normalize+startsWith containment check; legitimate filenames resolve and behave identically to before, ESAPI-encoded response message preserved.

R336.note: Removes shell invocation, execs traceroute with a fixed argv, and the hostname/IP allowlist regex anchors on an alphanumeric first character so it also closes leading '-' flag injection; restriction matches the endpoint's own domain (valid hosts) so no legitimate host is blocked.

R337.note: Removes the untrusted header value from the envp array entirely (Runtime.exec(args) falls back to inheriting the parent's environment, the standard default), eliminating the env-injection vector; the parameter served no legitimate purpose in the original code so nothing legitimate is lost.

R338.note: DOMPurify.sanitize(rawBody) run before bypassSecurityTrustHtml strips scripts/handlers/javascript: URIs while its default allowlist keeps <b>/<em>/<a>, matching the stated contract.
